extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in constitutional design, political reformers, legislators, and students of political philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and practical standards for framing constitutions and representative institutions — focusing on prudence, gradual reform, representation bases (territory/population/contribution), and the moral qualities required in lawmakers. Extracts standards Burke applies to evaluate the French Assembly's scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront and overcome difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulty is a 'severe instructor' and the glory of great masters is to confront and overcome difficulty; wrestling with difficulty 'obliges us to an intimate acquaintance with our object' and prevents superficiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value approaches that engage hard problems directly — they strengthen understanding and skill. Anti-pattern: evading difficulty via shortcuts, tricks, or superficial fixes which produce feeble, vicious, and insecure results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve what is useful when reforming
rubrics_metrics.description: To 'preserve and to reform' requires keeping useful parts of old establishments and fitting additions to what is retained; this demands steady attention, comparison and combination, and an understanding fruitful in expedients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer incremental adaptation that weights experience and tested institutions. Example guidance: watch effects of each step and proceed from 'light to light.' Anti-pattern: wholesale abolition and total destruction followed by naive rebuilding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberation, circumspection, and time as virtues in reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow, well-sustained progress is an excellence; time should be an assistant, and circumspection and caution are duties when altering the condition of sentient beings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reforms to be gradual so that each step's success informs the next. Avoid haste ('what your politicians think the marks of a bold, hardy genius are only proofs of a deplorable want of ability').

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawgivers should have sensibility and humility
rubrics_metrics.description: The true lawgiver ought to have 'a heart full of sensibility,' to love and respect his kind and to fear himself; he may apprehend ultimate objects intuitively but must act deliberately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate lawmakers on moral temperament as well as intellect. Anti-pattern: unfeeling, undoubting confidence presented as qualification for legislation (as Burke criticizes in Paris).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political arrangement must be effected by social means
rubrics_metrics.description: Political arrangement, being a work for social ends, 'is to be only wrought by social means' — mind must conspire with mind, and time is required to produce the union of minds needed for public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer consultative, deliberative processes that integrate multiple minds and experience rather than unilateral imposition. Avoid top-down engineering that bypasses social processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience and many minds improve plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience mends plans; those who take the lead are often improved by observations from those inferior in understanding; multiple minds over time are necessary for affairs that affect many generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include iterative feedback and broad consultation in constitutional design. Anti-pattern: heroic individual designers who refuse practical commentary and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix a presiding principle but allow it room to operate
rubrics_metrics.description: Best legislators often establish 'some sure, solid, and ruling principle' (a presiding principle) and then leave it to operate, combining a guiding rule with prolific energy in execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitute stable core principles while permitting gradual, practical implementation and adaptation. Avoid either atomized tinkering without principle or rigid templates applied without regard to consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid destructive novelty and sensational paradox as a mode of policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rousseau-style 'marvellous in life' and paradoxes may entertain, but practical imitation of such paradoxical rhetoric leads reformers to act imprudently; those who habitually find faults are unqualified to rebuild.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish literary devices from statecraft; do not convert rhetorical paradoxes into legislative programs. Anti-pattern: treating witty paradoxes as serious bases for policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware basing representation solely on abstract measures (geometry/arithmetic/finance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly's three bases — territory, population, contribution — are examples of relying on geometrical, arithmetical, and financial schemata that ignore moral and political realities ('Hominem non sapiunt').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design representative systems with attention to social relations, habits, and moral-political contexts, not only mathematical equality. Anti-pattern: rigid equal-area divisions or formulaic apportionment without empirical local knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial divisions must respect local habit and practical inconveniences
rubrics_metrics.description: Dividing territory into uniform districts (departments, communes, cantons) on geometrical grounds ignores local accidents, usages, and accommodations and will create innumerable local inconveniences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local knowledge and established practices when determining boundaries; a mere land-surveyor's partition is insufficient. Avoid purely geometric partitioning that severs historical and social ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for franchise based on property subvert equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposing qualifications (e.g., payment equating to days' labor) on voters or candidates contradicts the metaphysical principle of equal natural rights and establishes a 'tyrannous aristocracy' against the poorest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about property or tax-based thresholds for political participation; small-sounding qualifications may exclude those most in need of protection. Anti-pattern: charging the poor to exercise a right claimed as natural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layered representative stages with cumulative qualifications create barriers and oligarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple tiers — primary assemblies, communes, departments — each with separate qualifications for voting and candidacy introduce successive barriers that destroy independence and produce indirect aristocratic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether multi-stage electoral architectures and successive property/ contribution qualifications cumulatively disenfranchise or distort representation. Anti-pattern: designing tiers that multiply qualifications at each level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution-based representation risks creating an aristocracy of the rich and is hard to apportion equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation according to direct contribution admits a principle incompatible with personal equality and, even when applied to districts, produces paradoxes and inequities (e.g., rich individuals may be worse represented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the mixture of private and non-local causes of taxation/revenue; direct contribution is a poor local standard for political preference. Consider alternative measures and examine systemic incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect contribution (consumption duties) is a better measure of wealth than direct contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect contribution (duties on consumption) follows and discovers wealth more naturally than direct contribution, which is confounded by non-local phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using contribution as a metric for apportionment, prefer measures tied to consumption that more genuinely indicate local economic activity. Caveat: all such measures have limitations and must be interpreted carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making constitution dependent on mutable taxation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If representation or constitution rules are tied to how direct contributions are laid or apportioned, the constitution will vary with taxation and be inherently uncertain and unstable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insulate fundamental constitutional arrangements from short-term fiscal adjustments. Anti-pattern: designing constitutional franchise or representation formulas whose outputs swing with tax policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation should aim to reconcile diverse interests into a consistent whole
rubrics_metrics.description: A good system should 'compensate, reconcile, balance' so that various anomalies and contending principles in minds and affairs are united into a coherent composition rather than several contradictory principles forced together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate constitutional designs for internal consistency and whether they trade away important goods for others unnecessarily. Anti-pattern: cobbling incompatible principles together that 'claw and bite each other.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sever a nation into incoherent, essentially independent republics
rubrics_metrics.description: Partitioning into cantons/communes/departments that operate as nearly independent republics produces lack of cohesion and insufficient constitutional means of coherence, connection, or subordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve institutional links and subordination mechanisms between local and national bodies to maintain unity. Anti-pattern: creating many self-contained political islands with weak national integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess representation effects with concrete numerical examples (watch perverse redistributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Burke demonstrates by numerical hypotheticals how combining territory, population, and contribution rules produces absurd inequalities between cantons and communes (e.g., one urban canton with many voters sending fewer deputies than several rural cantons combined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use worked examples and computations to expose counterintuitive distortions; test apportionment rules with realistic scenarios to reveal perverse outcomes before implementation.
